messages:
alice.m: Quick q — going through a divorce, ex is asking for part of my 401(k) via a QDRO. Who do I loop in? Is there a vendor form? Do I need to pause contributions? Also I have an outstanding 401(k) loan — will that get offset? :worried:
sam_benefits: Sorry to hear that, Alice. Short answers: recordkeeper handles QDRO processing once we get a court‑signed QDRO. Legal should review the order. We don't auto-pause contributions — that stays with you unless you opt out. Loans: often netted/offset depending on plan doc. I'll loop legal, payroll, and the vendor. :white_check_mark:
jamie_legal: We can review the QDRO language. Key points: QDRO must identify the plan, specify alternate payee, and state the amount or % awarded. We don't draft QDROs for you but we will review and confirm it meets plan requirements. Send a redacted copy and the court-signed version when available.
tina_payroll: From payroll side — we only get involved if taxable withholding or reporting is required. If the recordkeeper issues a distribution/check to an alternate payee, payroll won't process that payment. If a loan offset becomes a taxable distribution, we'll coordinate tax reporting (1099-R) after vendor confirms.
vendor-ben: Hi all — recordkeeper note: once we receive a court-signed QDRO and plan admin approval, we typically process within 30–45 days. If the alternate payee requests a direct rollover to an IRA/plan, that can change timing. Regarding loans: outstanding loan balances are usually netted from the participant account prior to payment to the alternate payee; exact mechanics depend on plan doc. Please provide participant SSN (or last 4), DOB, and employee ID to match records.
alice.m: Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) What happens to employer match (vested vs unvested)? I got a match last month. 2) Do I need to notify anyone else now?
sam_benefits: Vesting follows the plan schedule. Whatever balance is vested at the time of division is treated as plan assets and split per QDRO. Unvested match may forfeit per plan rules — we'll confirm with the recordkeeper for your account. For now, just send the QDRO to benefits and cc legal.
jamie_legal: Also note tax implications: if the alternate payee accepts a direct rollover to another qualified plan/IRA, that portion is generally not taxable. If paid out to the alternate payee in cash, it's taxable to them and we report on 1099-R. We'll provide guidance language for the QDRO to avoid ambiguity.
alice.m: Great — practical next steps I can give to my ex's attorney?
sam_benefits: Ask them to reference our recordkeeper as 'ACME Recordkeeping' and include plan name (Redwood Inference 401(k) Plan) and employer EIN — send QDRO to benefits@redwood.com. CC jamie_legal@redwood.com and vendor contact ben@acme-records.com. Include court signature and payment instructions.
vendor-ben: To expedite review we need: PDF of the court-signed QDRO, participant full name and SSN last 4 (or full SSN if they provide securely), alternate payee name, and mailing address for any distribution. We will confirm acceptance or required edits within 5 business days of receipt.
tina_payroll: One more tax flag — if the loan offset amount exceeds $10k, it can be treated as a taxable distribution (per IRS rules) for the participant. We'll coordinate withholding/reporting once vendor confirms the processed amounts.
alice.m: Should I stop my contributions while this is processed?
sam_benefits: Generally keep contributing — stopping contributions can affect vesting and retirement savings. Only stop if you and your attorney decide it's necessary. We won't change deferrals without your explicit request.
alice.m: Okay, I'll get the QDRO scanned and send redacted copy now. Thanks everyone. :pray:
sam_benefits: Sending our standard QDRO checklist to you via DM, and we'll monitor the thread once the docs arrive. :thumbsup:
jamie_legal: I'll review once it's in. If you want, we can set a short call with your attorney to discuss plan requirements.
vendor-ben: Acknowledged — we'll stand by for the document and will queue it for priority review after receipt.
